correctness.rationale: Exhaustive and independent face predicates each return 3674 faces and 72 facets; opposite-order staged matchings each leave six critical 6-simplices and, after removing the augmented empty pair, one critical zero-cell. Two full directed Hasse topological sorts each visit all 3674 faces and include all 20940 incidences, certifying acyclicity; the resulting integral CW model is a wedge of six six-spheres. Signed reduced Lefschetz traces were computed for all 24 tetrahedral symmetries, giving (6,-2,2,0,0); the sign-twisted six-edge permutation character is exactly this and decomposes as sign + sign-standard + (2,2). All assertions are checked by the embedded standard-library verifier, whose exact output was replayed.

originality.rationale: Actual searches in research records and mathematical literature were compared against equivalent total cut, robust clique/Alexander dual, truncated-tetrahedron, and S4 representation formulations. Relevant foundational and newer papers were materially inspected. The closest exact-type symmetry computation concerns a different twelve-vertex cubic graph (hexagonal prism); the ordinary cut theorem for the same graph uses disconnected rather than independent triples and does not imply this result. No identified result has stronger coverage of both the exact homotopy and S4 character. Residual risk: an unindexed equivalent calculation.
residual_risks: An unindexed or otherwise inaccessible equivalent calculation could exist.

value.rationale: A canonical Archimedean cubic graph has a natural complete topological invariant: its pure eight-dimensional total three-cut complex retracts in homotopy to six six-spheres and is non-shellable. The new rational S4 action is the geometric orientation-sign twist of the six original tetrahedron edges, forcing zero invariant homology. This determines both an exact homotopy type and an independent symmetry-sensitive refinement, beyond a routine f-vector or a small numerical gain. The precise graph and representation are naturally motivated; no general/downstream theorem is asserted.
